title: Three-figure bearing of a cardinal or intercardinal direction
source: Theory IGCSE-15.2 Quick check 1 (west is 270); book three-figure bearings on printed p.476, new numbers
stem: A direction is \({k|int}\times 90^\circ\) clockwise from north. What is the three-figure bearing of this direction, in degrees?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The bearing is \({B|int}^\circ\) clockwise from north.
steps.note: B is 90k. Original k=3 is due west, bearing 270. k=1 east 90, k=2 south 180.

title: Back bearing when the given bearing is less than 180 degrees
source: Theory IGCSE-15.2 Quick check 2 (070 gives 250); book Worked example 2 style, printed p.477, new numbers
stem: The bearing of \(B\) from \(A\) is \({a|int}^\circ\). What is the bearing of \(A\) from \(B\), in degrees?

title: Back bearing when the given bearing is greater than 180 degrees
source: Theory IGCSE-15.2 Quick check 3 (215 gives 35); book tip on printed p.477, new numbers
stem: The bearing of \(B\) from \(A\) is \({a|int}^\circ\). What is the bearing of \(A\) from \(B\), in degrees? (If the three-figure bearing starts with a zero, give the number of degrees only.)

steps.name: A
steps.note: B is a-180. Original: 215-180=35, written 035 as a three-figure bearing.

title: Back bearing of 102 degrees

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2019), Question 8, including the official wording of the diagram. Official answer and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark.

stem:
This question is 0580/22/O/N/19 Question 8, taken from the official QP.

The diagram (NOT TO SCALE) shows a north line at \(B\), and a line from \(B\) to \(P\). The angle from north clockwise to \(BP\) is marked \(102^\circ\).

The bearing of \(P\) from \(B\) is \(102^\circ\).

Find the bearing of \(B\) from \(P\).  [2]

steps.name: M
steps.text_tex: The back bearing is \(102^\circ+180^\circ=282^\circ\), or equivalently \(360^\circ-(180^\circ-102^\circ)\).

steps.name: A
steps.note: MS Q8: 282 for 2 marks. Independent confirmation: 282.
